{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Sanofi) 
**Re:** Playbook review findings, RevMed collaboration agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Ten clauses are compliant (at or above the fallback) and require no redline. Eight items need attention: six deviations, one missing clause, and one critical indemnity item where our proposed redline did not pass verification and requires manual drafting review before it goes out.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us. The licence grant, IP package, termination-for-convenience right, exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, non-solicit, MFN, liquidated-damages and renewal positions all sit at or above our preferred or fallback positions — in several cases the restrictive covenants run against RevMed rather than us (e.g. the Section 3.5(a) SHP2 non-compete binding RevMed, and RevMed's post-termination royalty and inventory obligations).

The substantive gaps are risk-allocation gaps rather than pricing gaps:

- **Indemnity (critical).** RevMed's Section 14.1 indemnity does not cover third-party IP infringement/misappropriation arising from its services, deliverables or licensed technology, breach of Applicable Law, or RevMed-caused unauthorised access to our data. Because Section 13.5 disclaims any non-infringement warranty, 14.1(b) does not fill the gap. Our indemnity at 14.2 is materially broader than the playbook permits. Our proposed limbs (d)–(f) and the narrowing of 14.2 **failed verification** and must be re-drafted and re-checked before issuance.
- **Liability (medium).** Section 14.5 waives consequential damages but contains **no aggregate cap at all**, so direct liability is unlimited on both sides. This interacts with the indemnity point: the indemnities are currently uncapped, which is why we target the preferred indemnity position rather than a super-cap fallback.
- **Assignment (high).** Section 15.2(a)(ii) permits RevMed to assign the whole Agreement to an acquirer on a RevMed change of control without our consent, with no bar on assignment to a Sanofi competitor. Our outbound rights are already at preferred level and are retained.
- **Forum (medium).** Governing law is New York (preferred, Section 15.5). The forum fails both preferred and fallback: Section 15.6(a) mandates JAMS arbitration with seat and panel redacted and designates no court.
- **Warranty (medium) and transition (missing).** There is no performance warranty for RevMed's work anywhere in the Agreement, and Section 13.5 affirmatively disclaims anything outside Article XIII. Article XII's exit machinery runs one way only: we owe RevMed transition assistance and data/regulatory transfer; RevMed owes us nothing on general expiry or termination.
- **Audit (medium) and insurance (low).** Section 9.9 audit frequency, notice period and cost-shift trigger are all blank ([\*\*\*]) and there is an open-ended for-cause exception; Section 14.6 requires insurance but sets no monetary floors and no E&O or cyber coverage.

Separately, several key figures are redacted — the Section 12.2(a)(i) convenience notice periods, the Section 1.20 "Competing Product" criteria, and the Section 15.6 arbitral seat and panel. These should be confirmed against the unredacted execution version.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Needs review** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (14.1, 14.2, 14.3; cf. 13.5, 14.5) | No RevMed indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, or data breach; our 14.2 indemnity is broader than the playbook permits. **Proposed redline failed verification — re-draft required.** |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Intellectual Property Rights (3.1–3.4, 6.2, 10.1, 12.3(b)) | Meets fallback and most of preferred. Joint ownership of Joint Program Technology departs from the "no joint ownership" preference but is not walk-away given the unrestricted exploitation rights and perpetual cross-licence in 10.1(b). Noted, not redlined. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | General Provisions (15.2) | RevMed may assign to its acquirer on a change of control without our consent, with no competitor bar. Our own affiliate/successor rights are preferred-level and retained. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | License (3.1(a), 3.4(c), 3.5(a), 13.2(q); Art. VII) | No sourcing restraint on us; every "exclusive" provision runs in our favour. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (9.1–9.4, 9.6, 12.3(c), 12.6) | No LDs or penalties on us; only mutual late-payment interest capped at the legal maximum. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | License (3.1(a), 3.4; 12.3(b), 15.2) | At or above fallback. RevMed retains limited conditional termination triggers beyond material breach — noted, not redlined. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Term and Termination (Field §1.36; 3.5(a), 12.2(d), 15.2) | No non-compete or field restriction on us; the only such covenant binds RevMed. "Competing Product" (§1.20) is partly redacted — confirm criteria. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | Term and Termination (12.2(a)(i); 12.2(b)–(e)) | Unconditional convenience right for us, no lock-out and no termination fee; RevMed has no convenience right. Notice periods redacted; no pro-rata refund (payments expressly non-refundable) — noted only. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | Financial Provisions (9.9) | Frequency, notice and cost-shift trigger all blank, plus an open-ended for-cause exception. Independent-auditor and confidentiality elements already met. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | General Provisions (15.5, 15.6) | Governing law is at preferred (New York). Forum fails preferred and fallback: mandatory JAMS arbitration, seat and panel redacted, no court designated. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (14.5; cf. 14.6, 15.6(a)) | Mutual consequential waiver but no aggregate cap of any kind; direct liability unlimited. Indemnity and confidentiality carve-outs already present; gross negligence/wilful misconduct not carved out. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | License (Section 3 ROFN) | No Customer MFN; the only third-party-terms mechanic (SHP1-SHP2 right of first negotiation) burdens RevMed. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | Financial Provisions (9.1–9.3, 4.5(a), 4.2(a); 7.3, 12.5, 12.2(a)(i)) | All payment obligations are event- or usage-based; no minimum spend, volume cap or take-or-pay. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | General Provisions (15.1–15.9) | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | Term and Termination (12.1; 9.3(b)) | No renewal mechanic; single Term with early termination only. Rule structurally inapplicable. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | **Missing** | Term and Termination (12.3(c)(iv)–(vi), 12.3(e); 11.6) | Exit machinery runs one way only. No RevMed obligation to provide transition assistance or export our data on general expiry/termination. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | Art. XIII, §13.3 (Covenants by RevMed) | No performance warranty for RevMed's work anywhere; Section 13.5 disclaims all warranties outside Article XIII, so the gap is affirmative. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (14.6) | Insurance required "consistent with normal business practices" but no monetary limits, no E&O and no cyber/privacy coverage. |

### Proposed positions on the open items

| Rule | Proposal | Target |
|---|---|---|
| INDEMN | Add RevMed IP-infringement, breach-of-law and data-breach indemnity limbs (d)–(f), confined to RevMed's services, deliverables and the RevMed Licensed Technology (§1.99); narrow 14.2 to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law; retain 14.1(a)–(c) and 14.3 verbatim; keep the exception chapeau tied to limbs (a)–(c). | Preferred (fallback super-cap inappropriate while 14.5 is uncapped) |
| ASSIGN | Condition RevMed's change-of-control assignment on our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bar assignment to a Sanofi competitor. | Preferred |
| AUDIT | Cap audits at once per Calendar Year (delete the for-cause escape), require 15 days' prior notice, set the cost-shift trigger at 10% underpayment. | Fallback |
| GOVLAW | Move the merits forum to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County; strike the residual arbitration machinery (15.6(b)–(e) and the JAMS/award sentences) and narrow the 15.6(j) interim-relief carve-out. Preserve 15.6(f)–(i). | Fallback/preferred forum |
| LOL-CAP | Add a mutual cap at amounts paid or payable by Sanofi in the 12 months preceding the claim, subject to the existing 14.1/14.2 and Article XI carve-outs, with gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped. | Fallback |
| TRANSITION | Insert Section 12.3(f): 90 days' transition assistance from RevMed and export of Sanofi data within 30 days of expiry or termination. | Fallback |
| WARRANTY | Insert new Section 13.3(e): 90-day software-to-documentation conformance, 30-day services conformance, with repair/replacement or refund. | Fallback |
| INSURANCE | New Section 14.7: RevMed E&O of at least USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of at least USD 2,000,000; leave 14.6 mechanics intact. | Fallback |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

On the findings supplied, no clause was assessed as falling into walk-away territory. The joint-ownership feature of Section 10.1 was expressly assessed as **not** walk-away, given each Party's unrestricted right to exploit and license without accounting or consent and the perpetual, fully-paid cross-licence.

We would nonetheless treat the following as must-fix before signature, on the basis of the findings above:

1. **RevMed IP-infringement indemnity (INDEMN, critical).** With Section 13.5 disclaiming non-infringement and no indemnity limb for infringement, we carry unallocated third-party IP risk on RevMed's own technology and deliverables. This is the single item we would not close without.
2. **Uncapped direct liability combined with uncapped indemnities (LOL-CAP + INDEMN).** These two must be resolved together; a cap agreed without the indemnity limbs, or limbs agreed without a cap, leaves the package unbalanced.
3. **Unconsented RevMed assignment to a competitor (ASSIGN).** Nothing currently prevents the entire collaboration transferring to a Sanofi competitor on a RevMed change of control.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-draft the indemnity redline.** The INDEMN proposal failed verification and must not be circulated in its current form. We will re-draft limbs (d)–(f) and the 14.2 narrowing, re-confirm the cross-references to "Applicable Law" (§1.8) and "RevMed Licensed Technology" (§1.99), and re-verify that the exception chapeau remains tied to limbs (a)–(c) only.
2. **Confirm the two repaired redlines.** The AUDIT and GOVLAW edits were repaired during review; we will re-read them in situ before issuing, in particular the conforming changes to Sections 15.6(b)–(e) and 15.6(i)–(j).
3. **Request the unredacted figures.** Ask RevMed to populate or disclose: the Section 9.9 audit frequency, notice and cost-shift blanks; the Section 12.2(a)(i) convenience notice periods; the Section 1.20 "Competing Product" criteria; and the Section 15.6 seat and panel composition (relevant only if arbitration is retained).
4. **Issue a single consolidated markup** covering ASSIGN, AUDIT, GOVLAW, LOL-CAP, TRANSITION, WARRANTY and INSURANCE, holding the indemnity edit back only if item 1 is not ready; otherwise send all eight together.
5. **Sequence the negotiation.** Lead with the indemnity/liability package as one trade, then assignment, then the administrative fallbacks (audit blanks, insurance floors, transition, warranty), which we expect to be low-resistance.
6. **Do not open** the ten compliant clauses. Several sit above the fallback in our favour (licence scope, termination for convenience, RevMed's non-compete, one-way inventory and reverse-royalty obligations); reopening Articles III, VII or XII risks those positions.
7. **Business input requested** on the practical adequacy of a 12-month payments cap given the profit/loss-share structure, and on whether a 90-day RevMed transition-assistance window is operationally sufficient for regulatory and manufacturing handover."}
